_note: Scripted first-combat tutorial (end-of-M2). UI-only coach cards shown over the very first ship fight; dismissed once, persistently. Content is data so it can change without touching engine or UI code.

steps.title: Your first fight
steps.text: A ship has you in its sights. Ship combat is turn-based, and it's SIMULTANEOUS: you set up your whole turn, then hit Fire — and both ships act at the same instant. Let's walk the screen once.

steps.title: The enemy (top box)
steps.text: That's the ship trying to kill you. The coloured tag — GREEN, SEASONED, VETERAN, ELITE — is how dangerous they are. The bar is their hull; drop it to zero and they come apart.

steps.title: Your ship
steps.text: Below the log is your own ship and hull bar. If your hull hits zero, the run is over. You are not obliged to win every fight — Flee and Bribe are real options.

steps.title: Reactor power
steps.text: Your reactor makes a few power bars each turn. You divide them between Weapons, Shields and Engines with the − and + buttons. Each row reads allocated/max — the max is that system's level, and the three together can't beat your reactor pool. You can't power everything; that choice IS the fight.

steps.title: What each channel does
steps.text: Weapons power = how many guns can fire. Shields power = rebuilds your shield layers. Engines power = your dodge chance, and it charges your escape jump if you Flee.

steps.title: Your weapons
steps.text: Each weapon shows its type, its power cost (the ⚡ number) and its ammo (∞ = unlimited). Kinetics are cheap but bounce off shields; lasers strip shields away; missiles ignore shields but can be shot down; ion disables an enemy system without touching their hull.

steps.title: Red means it won't fire
steps.text: If a gun's power cost is higher than the power you've put into Weapons, its row turns RED and it will NOT fire that turn — the log will say so. Give Weapons more power, or don't target that gun this turn.

steps.title: Target, then Fire
steps.text: Tap a part of the enemy for each gun you want to fire — Hull to kill them, or Weapons / Engines / Shields to cripple them. Then hit Fire and both sides' shots resolve together. The ? Explain button up top repeats all of this any time. Good hunting.
